goal.goal: Deliver the implementation, executable test cases, verified review, and version-bound release manifest.
goal.user_contract: Implement solve(data). data is a list of {name: string, quantity: integer}. Normalize names with strip().casefold(); skip empty normalized names. Negative quantity raises ValueError, including on skipped names. Aggregate quantities by normalized name and return sorted [{name: normalized_name, quantity: total}]. Preserve zero totals. Empty list returns []. Do not mutate input.

permitted_outputs.contract: Python source exposing solve(data), implementing the user contract.

JSON list of at least four distinct test inputs. Each case has input plus exactly one of output (the expected JSON result) or error (exception class name). Descriptive extra fields such as name or notes are allowed and ignored by execution. Test expectations must match the user contract.

JSON object: candidate_hash (module.py sha256), tests_hash (test_cases.json sha256), verdict (pass or fail), notes (string). A pass review requires an actual successful run_tests receipt for these versions.
JSON object: candidate_hash (module.py sha256), tests_hash (test_cases.json sha256), review_hash (review.json sha256). All refer to the delivered file versions.

goal.receipt_terms: A pass review requires a genuine successful test receipt bound to the delivered module.py and test_cases.json versions. Receipts are returned to the session that ran the tests; there is no tool for retrieving a receipt issued by another session.

action.task: Write module.py and test_cases.json for the user contract. module.py: define solve(data) using only standard-library imports if any. For each item in data, normalize name with strip().casefold(); if the normalized name is empty, skip it. Check every item's quantity before skipping: a negative quantity raises ValueError, including for skipped names. Sum quantities per normalized name. Return a list of {"name": normalized_name, "quantity": total} sorted by name, preserving zero totals. An empty input returns []. Do not mutate the input. test_cases.json: a JSON list of at least four distinct cases. Each case has "input" plus exactly one of "output" (expected JSON result) or "error" (exception class name such as "ValueError"). Optional fields such as "name" or "notes" are allowed. Cover: normal aggregation, whitespace and case normalization, skipped empty names, zero totals kept, negative quantity error, negative quantity on a skipped name raising error, and empty input. Expectations must match the user contract exactly.
